newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House takes step toward Mexico censure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House takes step toward Mexico censure.

text.p: In a step toward final action on the issue, the House of Representatives on Thursday voted to overturn a finding that Mexico is a U.S. ally in the war on drugs but give it 90 days to improve its performance.

The House approved an amendment to the final resolution, providing that Mexico's black-listing would not take effect if President Bill Clinton reports within 90 days that he has "reliable assurances of substantial progress" by Mexico as a reliable drug-war ally.

The measure, approved by a vote of 212-205, was an amendment to a resolution adopted by the House International Relations Committee and awaiting final action. Clinton, a Democrat, has threatened to veto any effort to overturn his certification of Mexico as a drug-war ally.

The basic resolution would attempt to soften the impact of any decertification by waiving the economic sanctions usually required. These include a ban on U.S. aid and a requirement that the United States vote against loans to Mexico by international financial institutions.
Clinton last month certified Mexico despite charges by congressional critics that its government was riddled with corruption that compromised its effectiveness in the drug war.

Mexico has expressed indignation at the U.S. political debate over its integrity and has promised unspecified retaliation if the black-listing resolution passed. Even if the House did approve it, the measure also requires approval by the U.S. Senate where moves at a compromise were afoot.
